clue.text: Crazy, me, about a Frenchwoman

blocks.note: mad means crazy
the A of the definition's 'a' is shared, with ME after it

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are crazy about a woman from France.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is loose: MAD, then A and ME together, with 'about' meaning 'concerning'; the 'a' doubles as part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French courtesy title for a married woman, so it stands for a Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Record label millions love, tenor's first to admit

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word tenor

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for millions
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the opening letter of tenor
to own up is to admit

explanation.surface: A record company loved by millions, with a tenor the first to own up to liking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is the Detroit soul record label founded by Berry Gordy.

clue.text: Put off cleaner gent jilted

indicators.note: someone jilted is dropped by a partner, so that word is thrown out of the longer one

blocks.note: a detergent is a cleaning agent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is put off by a gentleman who has jilted her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' reads as a person, but it is the product DETERGENT, from which GENT is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage or put them off doing something.

clue.text: Handwritten document, with tear, kept in blessed sanctum

indicators.note: blessed is used here as a mild curse word, as in 'damned', suggesting the letters are messed up
kept in means held inside something else, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a rip is a tear

explanation.surface: An old handwritten text, torn, is kept safe in a holy inner room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blessed' looks like praise for the sanctum, but it works as a euphemistic curse signalling a reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript is literally a document written by hand, from Latin manu scriptus.

clue.text: Make a mistake rotating students

indicators.note: rotating turns the word round so it is read from the other end

blocks.note: pupils are students

explanation.surface: A teacher errs when moving students from class to class.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip up is an idiom for making an error.

clue.text: Hideaway left warm and dry

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
to air clothes is to warm and dry them

explanation.surface: A hideout that was abandoned in a warm, dry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, but it is just L. Airing laundry means warming and drying it, often in an airing cupboard in British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is an animal's den or a person's secret retreat.

clue.text: Model that's changed inside as fast as possible

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the previous word take a new order
inside places the reworked letters within the other word

blocks.note: to model is to pose, as for an artist
the letters of the word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A model who has had a costume change inside in record time.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste is an adverb meaning with great speed, from the old instruction on urgent letters.

clue.text: Drama in gym - gentry involved

indicators.note: involved suggests something tangled and complicated, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
the letters of the word, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spot of theatrical trouble in a gym where posh people are involved.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is the British school name for physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer Gynt is Ibsen's verse play, so it is an example of a drama.

clue.text: Huge movie

blocks.note: first meaning: colossal, gigantic
second meaning: the 1997 James Cameron film about the doomed liner

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a blockbuster; in fact the adjective and the film title are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means of enormous size, after the Titans, and is also the title of a famous film.

clue.text: Opposite number's bar role

blocks.note: a counter is a bar where drinks or goods are served
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: Your opposite number plays the role of barman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpart is a person holding the equivalent position elsewhere, which is what an opposite number is.

clue.text: A series under discussion

blocks.note: taken as written
a tissue is a connected series, as in a tissue of lies

explanation.surface: A set of episodes currently being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being debated, so it is under discussion.

clue.text: Film a number entertaining Irish press

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests holds them within, so the outer pieces surround the others

blocks.note: taken as written
IR is the abbreviation for Irish
to press someone is to force them
one is a number

explanation.surface: A group of performers entertaining journalists from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' acts as a two-part shell: 'press' looks like journalists, but it is a verb meaning to compel.
explanation.definitionFit: Air Force One is a 1997 Harrison Ford thriller named after the US presidential plane.

clue.text: Name old-fashioned puzzle

blocks.note: a word is a name for something
square is slang for conventional or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Naming a puzzle that has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A word square is a grid of letters reading the same words across and down, a type of puzzle.

clue.text: Gorilla may be hot on board vessel

indicators.note: something on board a ship is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a tug is a small vessel that tows ships
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A gorilla on a ship might feel overheated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorilla' looks like the ape but is slang for a heavy, a hired tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla in slang is a brutish heavy or minder, the same sense as a violent thug.

clue.text: Novelist in infamous bar in the north-east

indicators.note: in the means placed inside the compass points that follow

blocks.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east
evil and infamous both describe wicked notoriety
to bar a door is to shut it

explanation.surface: A writer found in a notorious pub in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevil Shute was the English-Australian author of A Town Like Alice and On the Beach.

clue.text: No North Sea oil? That's confused naval man

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled reaction to news that the North Sea has no oil left.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral killed at Trafalgar, the most famous sailor in the Royal Navy.

clue.text: Hospital in the Alps, newly-built with a fitness centre

indicators.note: something newly built is put together in a fresh form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
the letters of these words, to be rearranged with the a that follows
taken as written, added to the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A new hospital in the Alps with a gym attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A health spa is a resort offering exercise and treatments, a kind of fitness centre.

clue.text: Evaluating a small saw

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: Assessing a little cutting tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the cutting tool, but it is the noun for a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaying is testing metal for its purity, so it is evaluating its quality.

clue.text: Training on second musical instrument, a fiddle?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the training word follows the other pieces in the answer

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a harp is a musical instrument
practice is training

explanation.surface: Practising a second instrument, perhaps a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a violin but is a swindle; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is dishonest dealing, and a fiddle is British slang for a cheat or swindle.

clue.text: Behind adult not inclined to leniency

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
someone stern is strict and unforgiving

explanation.surface: Behind every strict grown-up there is someone unwilling to be lenient.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical word meaning at or towards the back of a ship.

clue.text: A stake in Italian tearoom

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A gambling bet placed in an Italian café.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake each poker player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: They may be put on for the rest of the train travellers in France, perhaps

definitions.text: They may be put on for the rest of the train travellers in France, perhaps

blocks.clueFragment: They may be put on for the rest of the train travellers
blocks.note: surface reading: extra carriages added for the remaining passengers
setter's reading: rest is sleep, and these are the sleeping cars attached in France

explanation.walkthrough: 'The rest' reads as 'the remainder', but it means sleep; the French phrase means sleeping carriages, lits being beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagons-lits are the sleeping cars of continental European trains, coupled on for passengers to sleep.

clue.text: Crazy discarding spades? Senseless

indicators.note: discarding means throwing away, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: insane means crazy
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card player foolishly throwing away spades.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and lacking sense, so it fits senseless.

clue.text: Solid fuel all right in church

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Using solid fuel to heat a church is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is the solid fuel left when coal is heated without air.

clue.text: Trendy type seen round hotel, briefly

indicators.note: seen round means one piece wraps about another

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a sort is a type
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A fashionable person spotted near a hotel for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: In short is an idiom meaning to put it concisely.

clue.text: Inform editor, surprisingly acute

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement of the following letters

blocks.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor
the letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling an editor who turns out to be unexpectedly sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate is to teach, giving knowledge, so it can mean to inform.

clue.text: Good parties for French wine

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
raves are lively parties

explanation.surface: Good parties call for French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux region producing red and white wines bearing its name.

clue.text: Small number crossing river, British one

indicators.note: crossing means lying across something, so one piece takes in the other

blocks.note: seven is a small number
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A few people wading across a British river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' in 'British one' points back to river: the answer is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England.
